title: Kestrel ransomware: the first six hours
debrief: Contain first, keep the evidence, report on time, and say only what you know. Decisions about paying belong to leadership with legal advice, never to one person under pressure.

s1.title: 09:55 Monday
s1.text: The helpdesk pulled hr-pc07's network cable at 09:52. Files on the HR share now end in .kestrel-locked and there is a README_RESTORE.txt in every folder.

choices.text: Isolate the HR share and the file server from the network, keep them powered on
choices.note: Stops the spread and keeps memory and logs for the investigation.

choices.text: Shut down every server in the building to be safe
choices.note: It stops the spread but loses memory evidence and stops the whole business.

choices.text: Restore the HR share from last night's backup straight away
choices.note: The attacker may still be inside. Restoring now can reinfect clean data.

s2.text: The share is isolated. The logs show a scheduled task and a new local admin account on hr-pc07.
s2.inject: The MD forwards an email from the attackers: pay 8 BTC within 48 hours or the HR files are published.

choices.text: Start the incident log, preserve hr-pc07 and fs01 images, and brief the MD with facts only
choices.note: Evidence first and a calm, factual briefing.

choices.text: Reply to the attackers to ask for proof that they have the files
choices.note: Only a trained negotiator, with legal advice, should ever reply.

choices.text: Delete the new admin account and the task right away
choices.note: Useful, but record and preserve them first, or you destroy evidence.

s2b.text: The restore finished, but at 10:31 the new files were encrypted again. The attacker's task is still on hr-pc07.

choices.text: Isolate everything now and start the incident log

s3.text: Payroll, offer letters and staff directory files were on the encrypted share. Some may have been copied out before encryption.

choices.text: Report to CERT-In within six hours of noticing the incident, with what is known so far
choices.note: CERT-In's 2022 Directions require reporting within 6 hours of noticing it. You can send updates later.

choices.text: Wait until the investigation is complete before reporting anything
choices.note: That misses the 6-hour window. Report what you know and update later.

choices.text: Ask the IT supplier whether they think it needs reporting
choices.note: The duty is yours. Decide with legal, quickly.

s4.text: Staff are asking what happened. A journalist calls reception.
s4.inject: Legal asks whether personal data of staff has been breached and who must be told.

choices.text: Tell staff the facts you are sure of, what you are doing and when the next update is; give the journalist a short holding statement
choices.note: Honest, brief and on a schedule.

choices.text: Tell staff it was a power fault while you work it out
choices.note: False statements destroy trust and can break the law.

choices.text: Say nothing to anyone until it is fixed
choices.note: Silence lets rumours fill the gap.

s5.text: Backups from Sunday night are clean and were stored offline. The attacker came in through the invoice email.

choices.text: Rebuild hr-pc07, rotate passwords, restore the share from the clean backup, block the indicators, and plan a lessons-learned meeting
Pay the ransom so the files are not published
choices.note: Paying funds crime, may break sanctions rules, and doesn't guarantee anything. Leadership decides with legal advice.
